tagline: High plains, a painted mesa, and scuba diving in the desert.
intro: Tucumcari takes its name from the mesa just outside town, where residents have painted a letter T on the hillside. From there the byway's roads fan out across the high plains: northwest on NM 104 to Conchas Lake, out to Ute Lake near Logan, up NM 469 south of San Jon onto the mesalands, and as far west as Santa Rosa and Pastura on US 54.
Some of these towns began with the railroad. Pastura was a water stop for steam trains, fed by a 142-mile wooden pipeline, and faded once the diesels no longer needed it.

moments.title: Blue Hole
moments.text: A bell-shaped artesian pool at Santa Rosa, more than 80 feet deep and a steady 62 degrees, where divers at 4,616 feet figure their stops from high-altitude tables.

moments.title: Caprock Amphitheatre
moments.text: South of San Jon, NM 469 climbs to the top of the mesalands, and up there is the entrance to the amphitheatre and the Ralph Stanfield Memorial Nature Trail.

moments.title: Conchas Lake
moments.text: Twenty-five miles of reservoir behind a dam the Army Corps of Engineers finished on the Canadian River in 1939, with a seaplane base two nautical miles to the north.
